newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Senate approves TV decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy Senate approves TV decree.

text.p: The Italian Senate (upper house) on Thursday approved a decree extending current laws on television ownership until January 31, 1997.

Without the move, magistrates could have forced former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi to take one of the three stations he controls off the air. A December 1994 ruling said no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three channels.
Thursday's decree was passed by 179 votes to 39 with five abstentions. It now goes to the lower Chamber of Deputies.

Deputies from the Greens party, which is part of the centre-left government, voted against the decree as did the hardline Communist Refoundation and Northern League parties which lie outside the two main blocs.
The government issued the decree in August, the day after expiry of a deadline set by Italy's constitutional court for a new legal framework on ownership to be in place.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said there will be no further extensions after January 31.

The government in July presented a controversial media bill to shake up the sector but debate on the bill, which will also establish a telecommunications watchdog, has been held up by parliamentary filibustering.
